* Shaykh: Did it not come in these benefits?
* Student: Some people consider it unlikely (...) they consider the answer unlikely (...) the sins (...) Iblis (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, this is for a wisdom, not out of compassion for Iblis. This is in reality from the wretchedness of Iblis, because the longer he remains, the more evil increases upon him, since upon him is the sin of whoever he misguides. Although this comes under the benefits, this is an answer that has been obtained, praise be to God. We must simply not submit to despair.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: "When will the help of Allah come?"﴾ up to this point, ﴿until the Messenger says﴾. In another reading: ﴿until the Messenger says﴾. That is, to the point that the Messenger, who is the most certain of people, says: ﴿When will the help of Allah come?﴾, meaning they seek victory hastily and are not patient. ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾ [al-Baqarah 214]. For this reason, we must believe that whenever a crisis and distress intensify, it is closer to relief.

But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿That, and if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them; but [He ordained fighting] to test some of you by means of others﴾ [Muhammad 4]. Allah is able, in a single moment, to take vengeance on them and destroy them all, but He tests some of you by others, and people are sinners. ﴿Thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, for what they used to earn﴾ [al-An'am 129].

These punishments occur because of sins that people have committed boldly over long periods of time. For example, if we look now at some countries that have been suffering for many years, with blood flowing in their markets, it is because they persisted for long periods in disobedience to Allah. It has reached us that a man among them, when he finishes his bread, throws it on the ground and tramples it with his foot, may Allah protect us. They trample oranges, apples and other fruits with their feet and play with them as one plays with a ball. And look at what has happened now! Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will deal with everyone who is arrogant toward His worship and ungrateful for His blessings, because Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, does not care for anyone. There is no favoritism, kinship or lineage between Him and anyone, so that He would say: "This one I favor, and this one I have mercy on." When punishment comes, it encompasses the righteous and the wicked alike, just as we passed over yesterday in the afternoon lesson, regarding the army that marches against the Ka'bah: "When they reached a barren stretch of the earth, they were swallowed up, all of them." 'Aishah asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, among them are their markets, and such-and-such, and such-and-such people who did not intend this matter." He said: "They will be swallowed up together, but they will be resurrected according to their intentions" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2118), and Muslim (2884/8), from the hadith of 'Aishah].

The conclusion is that this assumption that supplication will not be answered, which occurs among people, is an error on the part of the person. Rather, he should persist and repeat, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is near and responsive.

* A student: His saying: ﴿Were you among the exalted?﴾ [Sad 75]. That is, some of the angels had not received the news of the prostration to Adam.
* The Shaykh: No. ﴿Among the exalted﴾ refers to rank, not to place.
* The student: That is, I heard some of the exegetes say that it is...
* The Shaykh: No, that is not correct.
* Student: The hadith: "The sun and the moon are two oxen rolled up in the Fire" [al-Tayalisi (2217), and Abu Ya'la (4116), from the hadith of Anas].
* The Shaykh: "'Aqīrān" is correct. This is not a punishment for them; it is a humiliation for their worshippers. Everything that is worshipped besides Allah will be thrown into Hell as a humiliation for its worshippers. It will be said: "This is your lord whom you worshipped; look at him in the Fire." Even Hubal, al-Lat and Manat will all be in the Fire, although they are not accountable, but as a humiliation to the worshippers. It is like if we overpowered the disbelievers, brought their leader, and said: "This is your leader," then struck him, reproached him and humiliated him. This is a humiliation for them.
* The student: In His saying: ﴿with My two hands﴾ [Sad 75], here, concerning David, peace be upon him...
* The Shaykh: The hands.
* The student: (...)
* The Shaykh: Does Allah have only two powers? I say: He has only two (...). Power is derived from His saying "created," because only one who is capable creates. As for "with My hands," it is beyond the limit of creation. (...)

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say: "I am only a warner, and there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer"﴾ [Sad 65].

* In this verse, among the benefits: the command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to proclaim his message, through His saying: ﴿Say: I am only a warner﴾.
* Among its benefits: in speech one should consider the situation, since the context here is one of threat; therefore he limited himself to warning only, although Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾ [al-Baqarah 119].
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's oneness in divinity and the negation of it from anything else, through His saying: ﴿and there is no god except Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits: names do not change the realities they name. There are those who are called "god," but in truth they are not God.
* A consequence of this benefit: if we name a forbidden thing with a permissible name, the ruling on it does not change. Therefore, a hadith states: "Among my nation there will be people who drink wine, calling it by other than its name" [Abu Dawud (3688), and Ibn Majah (4020), from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari]. This indicates that names do not change the named things or their realities.
* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's unity through His saying: ﴿the One﴾.
* Among its benefits: a refutation of the Christians who say that Allah is the third of three.
* A consequence of this benefit also: their religion is false, I mean the religion they now profess, because 'Isa, peace be upon him, could not possibly have brought multiple gods. Therefore Allah will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Did you say to people: "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"? He will say: "Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not say to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them"﴾ [al-Ma'idah 116, 117], to the end of the verse.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's complete subjugation, the Mighty and Majestic, through His saying: ﴿the Subduer﴾. This necessarily requires that the believer fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His subjugation. It also necessarily strengthens the believer who trusts in Allah against his enemies, because when you trust that Allah is the Subduer, and that Allah is with you because you have acquired the attributes that warrant Allah's companionship, this strengthens you against your enemy, and you know that this enemy must be subdued by the subjugation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾ [Sad 66]. In it is the affirmation of the comprehensive lordship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through His saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, because the heavens, the earth and what is between them are the whole creation that we know of. Perhaps the Throne and the Kursi are included within the heavens in terms of elevation.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, ﴿the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾, and the affirmation of the attributes they contain, both together and separately, namely might and forgiveness. And that might and forgiveness together are stronger, more powerful and greater in perfection of might and forgiveness.

Then He said: ﴿Say: "It is a great news. You are turning away from it"﴾ [Sad 67, 68].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the greatness of what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought of revelation, and that it is a great news. This is like His saying: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news, over which they are in disagreement﴾ [al-Naba' 1-3].
* Among its benefits: whenever this news is great, the one who takes hold of it is great, because it is a foundation, a method and a path. When he is great, the one who takes hold of it is great. Therefore the Islamic nation was great, esteemed and awe-inspiring when it was holding fast to it.
* Among the benefits of this verse: a rebuke of those who turn away from this great news, through His saying: ﴿You are turning away from it﴾, meaning, how is it fitting for you to turn away from it when it is a great news?!

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they were disputing﴾ [Sad 69]. In this verse is the negation of the Messenger's (ﷺ) knowledge of the unseen, whether it is future or present but hidden from him. Because His saying: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly﴾ [Sad 69] is a negation of knowledge of an assembly that exists but is hidden from him. If he does not know what is hidden from him even though it exists, then what is unknown and awaited is even more so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the exalted assembly, which is the angels.
* Among its benefits: the explanation of the high rank of the angels, just as their place is also high, because they are in the heavens, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾ [al-Najm 26]. Scholars have differed regarding the elevation of rank among them: are they higher than righteous humans, or are righteous humans higher and more excellent than the angels? Some said the angels are more excellent, and some said the righteous humans are more excellent. The dispute here is of little benefit, because we know that the angels have characteristics that humans cannot attain, and humans have characteristics that angels cannot attain. So absolute preference is not valid, because these have one distinction and those have another distinction.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the angels are more excellent in terms of perfection of origin, because they were created from light, and light is more perfect and excellent than clay and dust. And humans are more excellent in terms of perfection of ultimate outcome, because humans will be in Allah's mercy, and the angels themselves will enter upon them from every gate, congratulating them: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured﴾ [al-Ra'd 24].

But what I see is that it should be said: the preference is not in terms of origin and outcome, but in terms of some characteristics that these have and those do not.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation that the angels are beings of intellect, through His saying: ﴿when they were disputing﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of debate and contention among the angels, just as it also occurs between the messengers and their peoples, and among the followers of the messengers with one another.

Then He said: ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner﴾ [Sad 70]. In this verse is the affirmation of the messengership of the Messenger (ﷺ), through His saying: ﴿It is only revealed to me﴾. Revelation comes to the messenger, and when it is revealed to him, it is that he should warn people and give them good news. But revelation sometimes comes as inspiration, as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee: take for yourself houses in the mountains﴾ [al-Nahl 68]. This is inspiration (ilham). And as in His saying: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Musa: nurse him﴾ [al-Qasas 7]. This too is inspiration, not revelation of prophethood and sending.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a warner.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation that he (ﷺ) makes clear everything he warned about, because what is the meaning of "mubin" (clear)?
* A student: The meaning of "mubin" is apparent.
* The Shaykh: No, that is the author's statement, but we have mentioned another meaning.
* Student: Manifesting.
* The Shaykh: Manifesting the truth and the revelation he brought.
* Among its benefits: it is impossible that there be anything unknown in the law of the Prophet (ﷺ) at all. Rather, everything he brought is clear. But ignorance is a relative matter. Something may be unknown to some people while it is clear and known to other people.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels﴾ [Sad 71], to the end of the verses. In these verses is the affirmation of speech for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through His saying: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: "Indeed, I am creating a human from clay"﴾ [Sad 71], and the affirmation that His speech is with an audible voice that the angels hear in this story, and the affirmation that it is with letters.

* Among the benefits of these verses: the affirmation that Allah creates, and that creation is related to His will, through His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human﴾, meaning, I will create him.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation that the origin of the children of Adam is clay. This is why the natures and colors of the children of Adam are varied, like the varieties of the soil of the earth: there is the easy and soft, the red, the white and the black, the sorrowful and the hard, because they were created from this soil. Thus their differences are like the differences of the origin from which they were created.

In it is also the affirmation that the children of Adam were created from clay. In another verse, they were created from dust, and in a third verse: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾ [al-Rahman 14]. There is no contradiction between these things or between these verses, because dust is the origin of clay, and clay is the origin of the sounding clay that is like pottery, since it is dust to which water is added and it becomes clay; it remains for a period and then hardens and becomes sounding clay.

* Among the benefits of these verses: the affirmation of Allah's actions, glory be to Him and exalted, through His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾ [Sad 72], and that His actions are related to His will, because "idha" (when) is a conditional particle indicating the future.
* Among the benefits of these verses: that Allah, the Exalted, perfected the creation of Adam and proportioned him, as He said: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin 4].
* Among its benefits: the honoring of the soul that was breathed into Adam, through His saying: ﴿and I breathed into him of My spirit﴾. This is an honor in two respects:
The first: that Allah is the One who breathed it, and He did not command any of the angels to breathe it.
The second: that Allah attributed this spirit to His sacred self.
* Among the benefits of the verse: that worship is obedience to Allah in whatever form it takes, even if it was forbidden at some point in time, through His saying: ﴿so fall down to him in prostration﴾. Prostration to other than Allah is shirk, but when Allah commanded it, it became obedience, and refusing it became disbelief.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the permissibility of making a command conditional, through His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾. A consequence of this is that if it is permissible to make a command conditional, then the thing commanded can also have a condition attached to its execution. Therefore the Messenger (ﷺ) said to Dubā'ah bint al-Zubayr when she complained to him about wanting to perform Hajj: "Perform Hajj and stipulate that your place of release is where you are held back, for you have from your Lord what you stipulated" [al-Nasa'i (2766), and al-Darimi (1852), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas].
* Among the benefits of these verses: that the angels are beings of intellect, so it is valid to address them and for them to carry out commands, through His saying: ﴿so fall down to him in prostration﴾. Then He said: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them﴾ [Sad 73].
* Among the benefits of these verses: that all the angels prostrated. Its apparent meaning is that the angels prostrated, not only those in the lowest heaven, nor those in the second, nor the third, nor the fourth, because the verse is general, and its generality is emphasized by two emphatics.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 38, verses 65–88 (part 4 of 5):

* Among the benefits of these noble verses: it is permissible for an address to be directed to a general group even if it includes someone who is not of that category. This is shown by His words: ﴿except Iblis﴾ [38:74]. Iblis was, without doubt, not an angel at all and not of their origin, but he was among them, so it is correct for the address to be directed to him. This is clear. If you ordered a group to prostrate and among them was someone who was not one of them, but who had their characteristics and acted in their manner, and then he disobeyed, you would certainly blame him, because the address was directed to all of them.
* Among the benefits of these verses: a name may carry the meaning of what it names. It appears that "Iblis" is an Arabic name derived from *al-iblās* (despair), because he despaired of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the condemnation of arrogance towards the command of Allah, by His words: ﴿he was arrogant﴾ [38:74].
* Among the benefits of these verses: arrogance towards the command of Allah is disbelief, by His words: ﴿and he was among the disbelievers﴾, meaning that through his arrogance he was among the disbelievers.
Some scholars have derived from this that the one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever, since if Iblis became a disbeliever by abandoning one prostration, then what about the one who abandons prostrations, bowings, standing and sitting? Indeed, this is not far-fetched. That is, using this verse as evidence that the one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever is not far-fetched.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the rebuke of Iblis for abandoning prostration to one whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, honoured and commanded to be prostrated to, by His words: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My two hands?"﴾ [38:75].
* Among their benefits: the speech of Allah, exalted is He, is connected to His will, since this statement was issued after Iblis's arrogance and his refusal to prostrate.
* Among their benefits: the affirmation that Allah creates, by His words: ﴿that which I created﴾.
* Among their benefits: the affirmation that Allah has two hands, by His words: ﴿with My two hands﴾. This is the dual form, which indicates that Allah, exalted is He, has two hands, and that is the case.
* Among their benefits: the honour of Adam, in that Allah created him with His hands and favoured him over others by this. However, the people of knowledge say that Allah planted the Garden of Eden with His hand and wrote the Torah with His hand.
* Among the benefits of these verses: a refutation of the people of *ta'til* (those who deny the divine attributes), who said that what is meant by "hand" is blessing or power. This is because blessing or power does not come in the dual form, since the dual form indicates restriction to a specific number, whereas the power of Allah is not restricted, and His blessings are also not restricted: ﴿And if you tried to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [16:18].
* Among the benefits of these verses, and especially this verse: the hands of Allah do not resemble the hands of created beings, because Allah attributed them to Himself, and what is attributed is according to what it is attributed to. Just as the essence of Allah is exalted and does not resemble the essences of created beings, so too are His attributes.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the use of restriction, or the method of *sabr wa taqsim* (enumeration and division), in debate and disputation, by His words: ﴿Have you become arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ [38:75]. It has already been explained that the meaning is: "Have you become arrogant within yourself while you are not worthy of exaltation, or were you exalted in your origin so that you would refuse to prostrate?"
* Among the benefits of these verses: the condemnation of arrogance, because the interrogative in His words ﴿Have you become arrogant?﴾ is for rebuke.
* Among their benefits: placing things in their proper positions, by His words: ﴿or were you among the exalted?﴾. This is because the one who is exalted over others cannot be lowered unless he is lower than others. Rather, everyone is placed in his own rank.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the clarification of the false claim that Iblis made in His words: ﴿He said, "I am better than him"﴾ [38:76].
* Among their benefits: a person may be blinded to the truth and then take as evidence what he is upon, supposing it to be in his favour, by His words: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: whoever gives precedence to reason over revelation is merely following the footsteps of Satan, because Satan gave precedence to what he claimed was reason over revelation and erred in that. Thus, everyone who gives precedence to reason over revelation, whether in matters of knowledge, which is the science of creed (*al-'ilmiyyat*), or in matters of practice (*al-'amaliyyat*), resembles Iblis and follows his footsteps. Know that every calamity that occurs from distorting words from their places, from arrogance towards the worship of Allah, and other such things, its root is from Iblis.
* Among the benefits of this verse: Iblis's acknowledgement that Allah is the Creator, by His words: ﴿You created me﴾ and ﴿and You created him﴾.
* Among their benefits also: Iblis had acknowledged that his rank was too low to be Lordship, by His words: ﴿You created me﴾, and a created being cannot be a lord.
* Among their benefits: Iblis knew the realities of the attributes of Allah better than many of the people of *ta'til*. Those who interpreted "hand" here as "power," if their interpretation were correct, Iblis would have said: "O Lord, I too was created by Your hands," because Allah created Iblis with His power just as He created Adam. But Iblis understood that what is meant by "hand" is other than power, and for this reason he did not deny Adam's distinction by his being created by the hand of Allah.
* Among their benefits: through his arrogance and refusal, Iblis became deserving of expulsion and removal, and for this reason it was said to him: ﴿So get out of it, for you are accursed﴾ [38:77].
* Among their benefits: when Iblis was expelled, he was further described as "accursed" (*marjum*), and stoning is more than expulsion.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Iblis is cursed, by His words: ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [38:78]. In another verse: ﴿And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ [15:35]. So shall we say that the absolute curse in His words ﴿upon you is the curse﴾ is the restricted one in His words here ﴿upon you is My curse﴾? Or shall we say that the curse there is more general, so that upon Iblis is the curse of Allah, of the angels, and of all people? This is possible. And this may be taken as absolute because it is more general, or we may take the absolute there to be restricted by the restricted here.
* Among the benefits of this verse: we do not invoke a curse upon Iblis, because he has already deserved this curse by the command of Allah, or by the information of Allah: ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse﴾. There is no need to say, "May Allah curse Iblis," because he is already cursed. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, commented on the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "Satan grows arrogant within himself when it is said, 'May Satan be cast down'" [Abu Dawud (4982), from a man among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)]. He said: such a thing, when one invokes a curse upon him, reviling him and the like, makes him grow arrogant within himself, meaning as if he had been unable to achieve it. So if he has already been cursed, there is no need for me to invoke it upon him. Rather, I should use what Allah commanded in His words: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾ [7:200]. Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not say to the Satan who attacked him during his prayer: "I curse you with the curse of Allah" [Muslim (542/40), from Abu al-Darda']? The answer: yes, but the Messenger (ﷺ) restricted it by saying, "I curse you with the curse of Allah," so he restricted it.
* Among the benefits of these verses: the affirmation of recompense, by His words: ﴿until the Day of Recompense﴾, where *al-din* here means recompense.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Allah answered Iblis's request and supplication, but not until the Day of Resurrection; rather, ﴿until the Day of the Appointed Time﴾ [38:81]. The Day of the Appointed Time is the day of the death of people, when the Trumpet is blown and they all swoon.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Allah may decree causes of evil for a wisdom, and this is by answering Iblis's supplication that Allah reprieve him until the Day of the Appointed Time. There is no doubt that Iblis is the origin of every evil, but Allah, exalted is He, let him remain for a great wisdom. Were it not for Iblis's remaining, no disobedient person would exist on earth, and if disobedience ceased, people would be one community, faith would have no distinction, there would be no jihad, no commanding of good, and no forbidding of evil. And if people were one community, many of the symbols of Islam would be neglected. So the wisdom lies in Iblis's remaining and in the remaining of what Iblis calls to.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Iblis's knowledge of Allah, in that he swore by the might of Allah that he would mislead the children of Adam, by His words: ﴿By Your might﴾.
* Among their benefits: one of the means of receiving help is that a person seeks help through the names and attributes of Allah that suit the situation. For he did not say, "By Your forgiveness I will mislead them," for that would not suit the situation, since he wanted to have power, and power is fitting with the attribute of might, not with the attribute of forgiveness.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Iblis knows some of the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, by His words: ﴿By Your might﴾.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Iblis made a promise, invoking the might of Allah, that he would mislead all the children of Adam.
It follows from this benefit that one must be cautious of Iblis and his whisperings. If someone asks, "What informs me of the whisperings of Iblis?", the answer is simple: everything that commands you to what is forbidden is from Iblis, and everything that holds you back from good is from Iblis. So beware! If you find in yourself a reluctance towards good, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. And if you find in yourself a readiness towards evil, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality﴾ [2:268].
* Among the benefits of these verses: the distinction of the sincere servants of Allah, in that they were saved from being misled by whom? By Iblis.
* Among their benefits: whoever is more devoted to Allah is more protected from Satan and his whisperings, because He made an exception from those Iblis would mislead among the children of Adam: the sincere servants. Whatever is attached to a quality grows stronger with the strength of that quality.
* Among the benefits of these verses: Allah, exalted and sublime is He, bestows His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants, making them sincere to Him, by His words: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them﴾ [38:83].
* Among the benefits of these verses: all the words of Allah are true, by His words: ﴿And the truth I say﴾ [38:84], where the object is placed first to convey restriction.
* Among their benefits: whatever Allah has decreed is true, whether it is agreeable to human beings or not. The reason is that everything Allah has decreed comes into being by His word "Be" [2:117], and "Be" is a word. If everything Allah says is true, then everything He decrees must be true, and so it is. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You" [Muslim (771/201), from Ali ibn Abi Talib].
* Among the benefits of these verses: Satan is in Hell, by His words: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾ [38:85].
* Among their benefits: Allah promised to fill Hell. From this benefit follows the utmost caution that a person should not be among the people of Hell; we seek refuge in Allah from it. It is established in the two Sahihs that Hell will continue to have people cast into it while it says, "Is there any more?", until the Lord of Might places His foot upon it, or His foot upon it, and then parts of it draw back into one another and it says, "Enough, enough" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6661) and Muslim (2848/37), from Anas ibn Malik].
* Among the benefits of these verses: Satan has followers, by His words: ﴿and those among them who follow you﴾. If it is asked, "Who are his followers?", the answer is: those who are arrogant towards the worship of Allah, because the greatest characteristic by which Satan is distinguished is that he is arrogant towards obeying Allah. Whoever is arrogant towards obeying Allah is a follower of Satan.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I of those who pretend."﴾ [38:86]

* In this verse there are the following benefits: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to announce that he does not ask for a reward for the message, meaning a worldly reward. As for the reward of the Hereafter, there is no doubt that the Prophet (ﷺ) hopes for it, because he is the one who guides to good and commands it. For this reason, the heirs of the prophets were prevented from inheriting any of their wealth, out of fear that it might be said that the prophets acquired it because of their message. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We, the company of the prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity" [Muslim (1761/56), from Abu Hurayrah]. Is it "charity" (ṣadaqah) or "charity" in the accusative? The word is definite: ṣadaqah. As for the claim of the Rafidah (a Shi'i sect) that it is read in the accusative, "We are not inherited from; what we leave behind is charity," this is a verbal and semantic distortion. This is because what is left as charity is not inherited, whether by prophets or by others. If a person bequeaths something to become charity after his death, it is executed and is not inherited, by the words of Allah: ﴿after any bequest he has made or debt﴾ [4:11]. However, whatever exceeds one-third is subject to the choice of the heirs.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not ask people for a reward for calling creation to the truth. Is this specific to him, or is it general for him and for his community? That is, is it forbidden for a person to take anything in exchange for conveying the Sharia?
The answer: whenever conveying is obligatory, taking a reward for it is forbidden, because it is not permissible for a person to take a wage in return for performing an obligation. But if it is not obligatory, there is no harm in taking a wage, because it is then voluntary: if he wishes he does it, and if he wishes he does not.
So if someone says, "I will not hold myself back except for a wage," we say: there is no blame, so long as conveying is not obligatory.
This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The most deserving of what you take a wage for is the Book of Allah" [al-Bukhari (5737), from Ibn 'Abbas]. But whenever teaching the Quran becomes obligatory upon a person, taking a fee for that teaching is forbidden.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is truthful in what he reports from revelation, by His words: ﴿and I am not of those who pretend﴾ [38:86].
* Among their benefits: an indication that among people there are those who fabricate against Allah, claiming to be messengers when they are not. In such a case we say: whoever claims to be a messenger, if he brings a sign that proves his truthfulness, then he is a messenger; otherwise he is not a messenger. This applies to what came before the Prophet (ﷺ). As for after the Prophet (ﷺ), whoever claims to be a messenger is a liar, because Allah says: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [33:40]. Whoever claims that Allah sent him after Muhammad (ﷺ) is a liar and an apostate from Islam, and it is obligatory to kill him. This is not refuted by the fact that 'Isa (Jesus) will descend at the end of time.

* * *

* The student: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
The Book of Clothing (*Kitab al-Libas*)
Chapter: the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants?"﴾ [7:32].
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Eat, drink, dress, and give charity without extravagance or vanity" [al-Nasa'i (2559) and Ibn Majah (3605), from Abdullah ibn 'Amr].
Ibn 'Abbas said: "Eat whatever you wish and wear whatever you wish, as long as two things do not befall you: extravagance or vanity" [Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah (25256), from Ibn 'Abbas].

* The Shaykh: Clothing is of two kinds: inner clothing and outer clothing. Allah pointed to both in His words: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment﴾ [7:26]. This is the outer clothing. What covers the private parts is the necessary clothing that cannot be dispensed with, and the adornment is clothing of beauty and ornament beyond the necessary clothing. Then He said: ﴿But the clothing of righteousness, that is best﴾ [7:26], and this is the inner clothing. As for outer clothing, the basic principle is permissibility, unless evidence has established its prohibition, because it falls under the general meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [2:29]. And because Allah rebuked those who forbid the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?"﴾ [7:32]. So whoever says to us, "This clothing is forbidden," whether because of its substance or its description, we demand evidence. If it is forbidden in its substance, he must produce the evidence for it. If it is forbidden in its description, meaning its cut, its embroidery, or its decoration, we demand evidence for that too.

If a person says: silk is forbidden, we say to him: bring the evidence. He will bring evidence for the prohibition of silk upon men. If a person says: wearing gold is forbidden, we say: bring the evidence, and he will bring evidence that it is forbidden for men. If a person says: silver is forbidden, we say: bring the evidence; but there is no evidence for the prohibition of silver in a general sense. If a person says: precious metals that are more valuable than gold and silver are forbidden to wear, we say: bring the evidence. The original ruling regarding everything that is worn is permissibility (al-asl al-hill), whether it covers part of the body or the whole body. However, two matters must be observed: the first is extravagance (al-israf), and the second is conceit (al-makhilah).

Extravagance (al-israf) is exceeding the limit, and it is a relative matter. Something may be extravagance for one people or with one man, while for others, or for another man, it is not extravagance. If a poor man wears the clothing of a rich man, it is extravagance, because he has exceeded the limit, for Allah says: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾ [At-Talaq 7].

Conceit (al-makhilah) is that a person intends by it arrogance (al-khuyala'), meaning elevating himself over people and showing that he has fine garments. Among this is dragging one's garment out of arrogance. If someone says: Is the use of what is good and beautiful in clothing included in conceit? The answer: No. If it has not reached the level of extravagance, it is not included in conceit; rather, Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, fine, wait except for the one who is hanging, yes.
* Student: How can giving charity involve extravagance and conceit?
* The Shaykh: Yes, what do you say? It may be that one is extravagant in it. He says: can charity involve extravagance and conceit? It may involve conceit, by giving much in charity so as to be seen; and likewise extravagance: perhaps one gives much in charity and reduces what is obligatory for the expenses of his family. If this interpretation is correct, it is clear; and if it is not correct, then his statement «without extravagance and without conceit» is to be understood as referring to other than charity.
* Student: The action of Abu Bakr.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: What supports that one who claims charity and extravagance is not one who gave away his wealth?
* The Shaykh: The action of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, may be explained as follows: he knew that his family would be content with that and would not demand what was obligatory, and the right belongs to them; so if they are content with it, there is no harm.
* Student: Do we not say: extravagance in charity, if a person needs dirhams and one gives him more than his need, so that this second person is corrupted?
* The Shaykh: That is considered from the perspective of the recipient, not the giver. There is a point to it, but it is not what is meant.
* Student: The one who does not believe the hadith about the fly says that this does not fall under (...). With what do we describe him?
* The Shaykh: We describe him as ignorant. It is obligatory for a Muslim, if a hadith is authentic, to submit to it.
* Student: If he is among those counted as people of knowledge?
* The Shaykh: Yes, we say: he is ignorant. Ignorance is of two kinds: compound ignorance (jahl murakkab) and simple ignorance (jahl basit). If this person is among those counted as scholars, and he denies what has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ, then he is undoubtedly ignorant.
* Student: Is it not an innovation (bid'ah), O Shaykh?
* The Shaykh: No, this is not an innovation. Something explicitly stated in the texts is not called an innovation. For example, we do not say to an adulterer, "You are an innovator." Everything the Lawgiver has explicitly addressed is not called an innovation.
* * *
* The student: Ismail narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Nafi', and 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, and Zayd ibn Aslam, who report it from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Allah does not look at one who drags his garment out of arrogance» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5783), and Muslim (2085 / 42)].
* The Shaykh: His statement «Allah does not look» — looking is of two kinds: a look of approval and mercy, and this is what is negated in this hadith; and a look of knowledge and awareness, and this is not negated, because nothing is hidden from Allah the Exalted; nothing on earth or in heaven is concealed from Him, and everything is encompassed by Him. But the look of approval and mercy is negated for one who drags his garment out of arrogance. The word "garment" here is singular and definite (mufrad mudaf), so it includes everything worn, such as a shirt, trousers, and a waist-wrap.
Do we say: and a cloak (mishlah)?
* Students: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, we say: and a cloak, yes. This hadith, as you see, has an explicit statement (mantuq) and an implicit meaning (mafhum). Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah does not look at him; and whoever drags it without arrogance, this threat does not apply to him, but another threat comes, namely «What is below the ankles is in the Fire» [al-Bukhari (5787) from Abu Hurayrah].
* Student: Whoever buys something forbidden, such as tobacco, while having only a small sum, can this be claimed to be extravagance?
* The Shaykh: No, this is not considered extravagance; rather it is considered a forbidden act, meaning poor conduct and foolishness, because extravagance is exceeding the limit and excess in a thing.
* Student: Dipping the fly is from the Sunnah.
* The Shaykh: For one who wants to drink it. As for one who wants to pour it out...
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, there is nothing wrong with that; this is the better course, and dipping it is undoubtedly the better course. The command here is one of guidance, so that the disease is met with the cure.
* Student: If the clothing is permissible, but it contradicts custom (al-'urf), does this count as evidence for prohibition?
* The Shaykh: Is the clothing permissible?
* Student: But it contradicts the custom of the land.
* The Shaykh: This falls under clothing of notoriety (libas al-shuhrah), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two kinds of clothing: the clothing of notoriety and the clothing of extravagance [al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (14136) from Ibn 'Umar]. So if a person wears something that contradicts the custom of the land but is not forbidden, it falls under the clothing of notoriety.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 38, verses 65–88 (part 1 of 5):

Then God the Exalted said: (﴿Say﴾ [Sad 65], O Muhammad, to the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿I am only a warner﴾.) As for ﴿Say﴾, there is no doubt that the address is to the Messenger ﷺ, and that it is an address specific to him, because the warning that is the warning of prophethood belongs specifically to the Messenger ﷺ.

As for the author's statement, "﴿Say﴾ to the disbelievers of Makkah," the reason for the specification is that this surah was revealed in Makkah before the Prophet ﷺ migrated. Therefore the command addressed to him to declare that he is a warner is specific to the people of Makkah.

However, it may be said that it is better to take it as general, and to say that the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion or the place.

(﴿Say, I am only a warner﴾, one who threatens with the Fire.) Whom? The disbelievers. So the warning of the Fire is for the disbelievers, and the good news of Paradise is for the believers. But the context here requires warning.

﴿And there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Sad 65]. This is a restriction of the highest kind, because it is built on negation and affirmation: the negation is emphasised by ﴿مِنْ﴾ (min) in ﴿And there is no god﴾, because ﴿مِنْ﴾ is an extra preposition, and the extra element in the Noble Qur'an adds to the meaning.

As for his statement, ﴿there is no god﴾, it means there is no true object of worship except Allah. Otherwise, there are gods that are worshipped, but they are not truly gods; they are merely names that their owners have named, for which Allah has sent down no authority. For this reason they do not worship them with true worship. When harm befalls them, whom do they call upon? They call upon Allah alone. Thus, by the tongue of their state, they testify that these gods, and the idols they worship, are not gods.

The point is that his statement ﴿there is no god﴾ means there is no true god, ﴿except Allah﴾, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿The One﴾ means the one who has no partner. ﴿The Subduer﴾ means the one who has no overpowerer, but rather is the one who subdues His creation. And ﴿al-Qahhar (the Subduer)﴾ here may be a relative form (nisbah), in which the doubling of the letter indicates attribution, and it may be an intensive form (for abundance), so that it is a form of intensification (mubalaghah). We may also say that it is both together: Allah the Exalted has as one of His necessary attributes that He is Subduer, and because of the number of tyrants He subdues, His subjugation is abundant. So this is for the relative form, what? And for the abundance called intensification.

﴿The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾ [Sad 66]. ﴿The Lord﴾ here is a substitute (badal) for Allah, and it may also be the predicate of an omitted subject, its estimated form being: He is Lord. As for ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, we have discussed them at length before. As for his statement ﴿and whatever is between them﴾, it means the great creatures that we know and that we do not know.

We have already mentioned that God's placing what is between the heaven and the earth as a counterpart to the heavens and the earth indicates the greatness of what lies between them of creatures, which we have not yet reached the end of.

As for his statement ﴿the Mighty﴾, the author said: "the one who prevails over His affair." This is one of the meanings of al-'Aziz (the Mighty), because al-'Aziz has three meanings: al-'Aziz in the sense of one possessing rank and honour; al-'Aziz in the sense of subjugation and dominance; and al-'Aziz in the sense of one who cannot be touched by harm, derived from "arḍ 'azzāz," meaning hard land that axes do not affect.

So ʿizzah (might) has three meanings: the might of rank, the might of subjugation, and the might of invulnerability, meaning that harm cannot reach Him, glory be to Him and exalted.

As for his statement ﴿the Forgiving﴾, it means the one who forgives much. We may also take it as a relative form, meaning that He is characterised by forgiveness always, so how many are those whom Allah forgives, and how many are the sins that Allah the Exalted forgives! Here He has joined might with forgiveness, which adds a third meaning beyond might and forgiveness: that despite His might, dominance and subjugation, He is nevertheless Forgiving. This differs from created beings who are characterised by might, where might may overcome their forgiveness, or those who are characterised by forgiveness, who may be weak and have no might. When might and forgiveness combine, a compound meaning results from their union, which is more complete than if either one stood alone.

* Student: (...) subjugation and might combined (...).
* Shaykh: "Subjugation and might" is an error.
* Student: Some people have might, but their forgiveness does not overcome their might, whereas Allah the Exalted, His forgiveness...
* Shaykh: What? We did not understand!
* Student: I mean, some people have might.
* Shaykh: And they have no forgiveness.
* Student: And they have no forgiveness.
* Shaykh: And some of them?
* Student: Some of them have might and have forgiveness, but less than their might.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Some of them have forgiveness and mercy, but they are weak and have no might.
* Shaykh: They have forgiveness but not might. The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, combines both of these. There is no doubt that the predominance of forgiveness over might contains a deficiency, and the predominance of might over forgiveness contains a deficiency. When both are together, this becomes more perfect; that is, His might, dominance and subjugation are never free of forgiveness.

He says: ﴿Say﴾ (to them), ﴿It is a great news. You turn away from it﴾ [Sad 67–68]. ﴿It﴾ means the news that I have informed you of, which I came with as a warner, is a great news. Naba' (news) means information, but it is used only for matters of great importance. God the Exalted says: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ [An-Naba' 1–2]. So naba' is information, but it is used for important matters. God described this news as ﴿great﴾, and it is the Qur'an. God has described the Qur'an as great, noble and glorious, because it possesses these qualities, and whoever adheres to it attains these attributes in proportion to how much he adheres to it.

﴿You turn away from it﴾ (that is, the Qur'an which I have informed you of, and in which I have brought you what cannot be known except through revelation).

His statement ﴿You turn away from it﴾ is a new independent sentence (jumlah istie'nafiyyah), intended to express the severity of the reprehensibility of these deniers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Despite this great news, they did not turn towards it, but turned away from it, did not pay attention to it, and gave it no weight.

He says: ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they were disputing﴾ [Sad 69]. That is, this great news could not have come from my own self, because I have no knowledge of ﴿the Exalted Assembly﴾, meaning the angels. They are called an assembly (mala'), but they are above, since their original dwellings are the heavens, though they descend to the earth to carry out the duties assigned to them.

(﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly﴾, that is, the angels, ﴿when they were disputing﴾ about the matter of Adam, when God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ [Al-Baqarah 30], and so on.)

The correct view is that the meaning of the verse is more general than what the author said; that is, "I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they were disputing about the matter of Adam, and about the high ranks, and other matters over which the angels dispute and refer back to Allah."

He says: (﴿in﴾; that is, ﴿mā﴾). The author informed us that ﴿in﴾ here is a negative particle, which is one of its meanings.

As for his statement ﴿It is only revealed to me that﴾: ﴿It is only that﴾ is what indicates that ﴿in﴾ is negative: ﴿It is only that I am﴾ [Sad 70] (that is, that I am) ﴿a clear warner﴾ [Sad 70]. His statement "that is, that I am" is an explanation of ﴿innamā anā﴾, because its original form is ﴿annī﴾ (that I), but the particle ﴿mā﴾ (the restrictive particle) entered upon ﴿an﴾ (that). When ﴿mā﴾ entered upon ﴿an﴾, it cancelled its government of the accusative. Isn't that so? Then, when it entered upon it, the attached pronoun had to become detached. Where is the attached pronoun? It is ﴿annī﴾; that is the original. We added ﴿mā﴾ to ﴿an﴾, so now there is a separation between ﴿an﴾ and the pronoun. When something separates an attached pronoun from what it is attached to, it becomes detached, because it was attached to its noun. When something separates it from what it is attached to, detaching it becomes obligatory. So here ﴿anā﴾ is the yā' in the author's words "annī."

﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner﴾ [Sad 70]. But when ﴿innamā anā﴾ comes, it is more emphatic in restriction, because the restriction is now derived from His statement ﴿It is only revealed to me that﴾ and also from His statement ﴿It is only that I am a clear warner﴾. Thus the state of the Prophet ﷺ is restricted to being a clear warner. This restriction, as you know, is a relative restriction (ḥaṣr idāfī), meaning that: in this matter specifically, which is revelation, I am a clear warner; otherwise he is a human who forgets, eats, drinks and gives good news. So the restriction is relative according to the context.

As for his statement ﴿mubīn﴾ (clear), the author said: "clarifying the warning." The correct meaning is: ﴿muẓhir﴾ (manifesting). ﴿It is only that I am a clear warner﴾ means manifesting, and it is not from the intransitive ﴿abāna﴾, but from the transitive ﴿abāna﴾. Because the word ﴿abāna﴾ can be intransitive, as when you say, "The dawn ﴿abāna﴾," meaning it appeared; and it can be transitive, as when you say, "This is ﴿mubīn﴾ for this," meaning it manifests it. So the correct view is that ﴿mubīn﴾ here means manifesting.

Then the author said: ("Mention") ﴿when﴾. He informed us, may Allah have mercy on him, that ﴿when﴾ is connected to an omitted verb, whose estimated form is ("Mention").

﴿When your Lord said to the angels: Indeed, I am going to create a human from clay﴾ [Sad 71] (he is Adam). As for his statement ﴿I am going to create a human﴾, ﴿a human﴾ is the object of the active participle ﴿creating﴾ in order to complete the conditions for its operation. ﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾ (that is, completed him), ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾ (that is, caused to flow), ﴿he became alive﴾, and so on. The author said: ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾, and explained it as "caused to flow." It seems that he, may Allah have mercy on him, interpreted the breathing as causing to flow. However, this contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse, which is that God the Exalted breathed into him of His spirit. We affirm this breathing according to its apparent meaning, but without it being like the breathing of created beings. Explaining it as "causing to flow" is an explanation by necessary consequence, because when the spirit is breathed into him, it necessarily flows through the body and spreads through it.

He said: As for his statement ﴿of My spirit﴾, the author said: "the attribution of the spirit to Him is an honouring of Adam." That is, ﴿of My spirit﴾ does not mean a part of Me, but rather it means of My spirit, that is, from the spirits that I created, and Allah attributed it to Himself as an honour and glorification, just as He attributed the House to Himself in His statement ﴿and purify My House﴾ [Al-Hajj 26], and as He attributed the mosques to Himself in His statement ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah 114], and as He attributed the she-camel to Himself in His statement ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you﴾ [Al-A'raf 73]. The thing attributed to Allah, if it is created, its attribution to Him is by way of honour and glorification if it is specific; but if it is general, it is by way of comprehensiveness and generality, as in His statement ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 13].

Then He said: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit﴾. The author said: "The spirit is a subtle body by which a human lives through its penetration into him." The spirit is a subtle body by which a human lives. If the author had said "by which a living being lives," it would have been more general, because humans have spirits, and so do animals.

As for the author's statement "a subtle body," that it is a body is established because the Qur'an clearly states that it is taken and made to die, and the Sunnah establishes that it is shrouded and wrapped in cloth, in the shroud, either from Paradise or from Hell. This indicates that it is a body, but it is a subtle body that is not seen with the eye. When it enters the body, it lives, and when it is lost from the body, the body becomes lifeless. We now observe something made by humans that resembles this: when you have a negative and a positive in electricity, and they connect with one another, they ignite, lighting up a large bulb, and this is something not seen with the eye; when they are separated, it is lost. This is from the making of humans, so how about the extraordinary matters that none knows but Allah? ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord﴾ [Al-Isra' 85]. And what the author explained the spirit by is the best of what has been said in explaining the spirit.

He says: ﴿So fall down prostrating to him﴾ ("fall down" is an imperative verb; its past is ﴿waqa'a﴾, and its present is ﴿yaqa'u﴾, and falling means "bow down to the earth") ﴿prostrating﴾. The author said: "a prostration of greeting by bowing."

As for his statement "a prostration of greeting," there is no doubt that this is what is meant, that is, not a prostration of worship. As for his statement "by bowing," there is room for consideration, because prostration is falling to the ground, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. However, it may be said that this prostration was permissible, and that prostrating to others as a greeting was permissible, but it was abrogated later (nusikha).

﴿prostrating﴾: what is its grammatical position (maḥalluhā min al-i'rāb)?
* Students: A circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).
* Shaykh: From where? From the subject in ﴿fa-qa'ū﴾ (fall down).

He says: ﴿So all the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ [Sad 73] (there are two emphatic words). They are ﴿kull﴾ (all) and ﴿ajma'ūn﴾ (all together).

﴿Except Iblis﴾ (he is the father of the jinn; he was among the angels). As for his statement "he is the father of the jinn," the evidence is His statement: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me?﴾ [Al-Kahf 50]. The evidence that he is from the jinn is His statement: ﴿Except Iblis; he was one of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord﴾ [Al-Kahf 50]. So the jinn are the descendants of Satan, and mankind are the descendants of Adam. We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.

He said: ﴿Except Iblis﴾ (he was among the angels). The author did not say he was from the angels, because God the Exalted said: ﴿Except Iblis; he was one of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord﴾ [Al-Kahf 50]. So he was among them, and whoever is among people is one of them. The Prophet ﷺ said: «Verily, the freed slave of a people is one of them»[[Reported by al-Bukhari (6761) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]]. This Satan, who was with the angels, worshipping as they worshipped, may be included in the address directed to the angels; for this reason Allah blamed him for not prostrating, which indicates that the address included him.

﴿Except Iblis, who was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ [Sad 74] (in the knowledge of Allah). As for his statement "in the knowledge of Allah," it is based on the view that ﴿kāna﴾ (was) indicates the past. However, it has already passed before us that ﴿kāna﴾ may be stripped of indicating time, and the intended meaning is the attribute of its predicate, as in His statement: ﴿And Allah has always been Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa' 96]. Does ﴿kāna﴾ mean it was in the past, or does it mean He is characterised by mercy? So in this verse we say: ﴿and was among the disbelievers﴾ means and was characterised by disbelief. There is no need to say "was in Allah's knowledge," because we say that ﴿kāna﴾ here is stripped of indicating time, so its intention is mere attribution.

﴿He said: O Iblis﴾: who is the subject of ﴿said﴾? Allah, because He said: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him﴾ and ﴿fall down﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 38, verses 65–88 (part 2 of 5):

﴿He said: "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?"﴾ [38:75] That is, "What prevented you?" This interrogative is for rebuke and astonishment, meaning: How can you refuse to prostrate to one whom I created with My own hands? God Most High created Adam with His hand, and this is an honour for him. He commanded the angels to prostrate to him as an honouring of him. So what prevented you from prostrating? The author (al-Mu'allif) said, in explaining His words ﴿with My two hands﴾: "(That is, I took charge of his creation, and this is an honour for Adam, since every creature whose creation God has taken charge of...)." May God forgive you, O author! He says: "I took charge of his creation," to flee from affirming a hand for God. Without doubt this is a distortion (tahrif). He also answered concerning the attribution in His words ﴿what I created with My two hands﴾ by saying that this is an honour for Adam, otherwise every creature is one whose creation God has taken charge of. According to the author's statement, Adam would have no excellence over the rest of creation, isn't that so? If we explain ﴿I created with My two hands﴾ as "I took charge of his creation," then God took charge of the creation of the children of Adam, of the camels, the cattle, the sheep and other things. Then Adam would have no excellence over anyone, indeed no excellence over Satan who refused to prostrate. For is it not God, Mighty and Majestic, who took charge of Satan's creation? For this reason we say to the author: he erred in this, and the meaning of the verse is that God created Adam with His hand, and created other than Adam, namely the devils and the angels, by His word (kun, "Be!"), that is, by His saying "Be." As for Adam, He created him with His hand, and this is the point of distinction and the special quality of Adam, that God created him with His hand.

(﴿Have you become arrogant now?﴾) (That is, against prostrating.) It is an interrogative of rebuke. ﴿Or were you among the exalted?﴾ (That is, among the arrogant, so that you became arrogant against prostrating.) That is, has arrogance occurred from you, which you are feigning while you are not of its people? ﴿Or were you among the exalted?﴾ meaning those whose rank is high. For the one who refuses either is in a higher position and so deserves to refuse, or he is arrogant, meaning his position is low but he has placed himself in a high station. So God says to him: Are you arrogant? Or are you exalted in a rank higher than Adam, indeed higher than the one who commanded you? What is the answer? He now claims: "(Among the arrogant, so you became arrogant against prostrating because you are of them)." Of whom? Of the exalted.

As for the author's statement, "(The exalted are the arrogant)," this leads to there being no distinction between the two parallel phrases. For if he says "Have you become arrogant, or were you among the arrogant?", is there any difference? There is none. Therefore his explanation of "the exalted" as "the arrogant" is considered an error. Rather, ﴿or were you among the exalted?﴾ means those whose rank is elevated such that no command to prostrate to one who is lower than them is directed at them. So Iblis's refusal to prostrate to Adam is either for a quality that he deserves, and this is indicated by ﴿or were you among the exalted?﴾, or for a quality he does not deserve, but he was arrogant and considered himself great, and this is in His words ﴿Have you become arrogant?﴾.

﴿He said﴾ Iblis, answering God's question: ﴿I am better than him﴾, than Adam. This is a claim, and every person who attributes something to himself is, as we have taken as a rule in jurisprudence (fiqh), a claimant (mudda'i), and the one against whom the claim is made must provide evidence (bayyinah). He brought evidence, namely his words ﴿You created me from fire﴾. For this reason we say: the sentence here is resumptive (istinafiyyah), explaining the basis of his superiority. ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [38:76]. Glory be to God! Is that which is created from fire better than that which is created from clay? Even though the fire from which Satan was created is not a bright flame? ﴿From a smokeless fire﴾ [55:15]. It is not the bright flame; it is the fire found at the top of the blaze, between the smoke and the bright fire, which is red and dim.

Is it the case that this creature made from this fire is better than the creature made from cool, beneficial clay? Glory be to God! This is an inversion of realities. For this reason we say: this is a claim supported by false and baseless evidence. Where is the claim? ﴿I am better than him﴾ [38:76]. The evidence: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [38:76]. This is not evidence; this is an argument against him, not an argument for him. The scholars have mentioned in this context the explanation that what Adam was created from is better than what Iblis was created from.

God Most High said: ﴿So get out of it﴾ [38:77] (that is, out of Paradise; it was said, out of the heavens). Which is closer? Are the angels all in Paradise? In the heavens. ﴿So get out of it﴾, that is, out of the heavens, is closer to the wording.

﴿For you are accursed﴾ (that is, "stoned"). It is the form fa'il in the sense of maf'ul. The meaning of "stoned" is expelled and removed, as a person is removed when he is stoned. You know that when we want to drive a man far away, we first shout at him, and if he flees, we pursue him with stones, and this is more severe in removal.

﴿And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgement﴾ [38:78]. Upon you is the right, the established right: the curse of God upon you, that is, His expulsion and removal. ﴿Until the Day of Judgement﴾ (the Day of Recompense). Does the curse cease after the Day of Judgement? It does not cease. But when it extends until the Day of Judgement, its meaning is that he is despairing of the mercy of God, may God protect us. He cannot be shown mercy. The one upon whom the curse remains until the Day of Judgement cannot attain mercy.

﴿He said: "My Lord, then give me respite until the day they are resurrected."﴾ [38:79] (That is, mankind.) ﴿He said: "Indeed you are among those given respite, until the day of the appointed time."﴾ [38:80–81] He asked God to grant him respite until the resurrection of mankind. Did God grant his request? God granted him ﴿until the day of the appointed time﴾. The author said: (The time of the first blast), that is, before the resurrection, because people are not resurrected except at the second blast; but they will swoon at the first blast. And Satan only wants to remain until there is not one left of the children of Adam, because he has come to have in himself a great rancour and hatred toward Adam and his offspring. How was he commanded to prostrate to him? And how was he judged to be a disbeliever when he refused? It became in his heart, or in his soul, something more; for we do not know whether he has a heart or not. There came to be in his soul rancour and hatred, so he asked God to let him remain until the day of resurrection. God answered him that he would remain until the day of the appointed time. God's granting of his request has great wisdoms, which we will mention, God willing, when we speak of the benefits (fawa'id).

﴿He said: "Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them."﴾ [38:82–83] ﴿He said: "Then by Your might, I will mislead them"﴾: the "ba'" may be for oath, and it may be for seeking help. If we say it is for oath, then he swore by God's might, and his choice of swearing by might is because might includes dominance, so he swore by an attribute of God through which dominance belongs to Him. If we say it is for seeking help, it is evident that seeking help through God's might, by which when God aids a servant, he prevails.

﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾: the lam in His words ﴿I will surely mislead them﴾ confirms that the "ba'" here is for oath, because this is the answer to the oath. And ﴿I will mislead them﴾ means: I will lead them along the path of error, which is the opposite of right guidance.

﴿Except Your chosen servants among them﴾, that is, among the children of Adam, ﴿the sincere ones (mukhlasin)﴾, whom You have purified. This is like His words: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the deviators﴾ [15:42].

God Most High said: ﴿So the truth is, and the truth I say﴾ [38:84] ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together﴾ [38:85]. He said ﴿So the truth﴾: this is a subject (mubtada'), but it contains the meaning of an oath, as shown by the fact that it has a predicate given as the answer to the oath, which is His words ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾. The author gave its i'rab (grammatical analysis), saying: (in the accusative for both). How? ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I say"﴾.

((And the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative.)) ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I say"﴾ ((So its accusative is by the verb after it, and the first accusative is said to be by the mentioned verb, and it is said to be as an absolute object (masdar), that is: "Let the truth be truth," and it is said to be by removing the particle of oath, and its nominative is that it is a subject whose predicate is omitted, that is: "So the truth is from Me." It is also said: "So the truth is my oath," and the answer to the oath is ﴿I will surely fill﴾.)) Multiple grammatical analyses.

(In the accusative for both.) We say: the second is accusative by the verb after it, which is clear: ﴿the truth I say﴾, because the verb after it has not completed its object, and we do not find an object for it except "the truth" that preceded. That is, the second "the truth" is in the accusative by "I say" in every case. The disagreement is about what? About the first. The first is either accusative or nominative. Its accusative has several possibilities: (it is said: by the verb mentioned), that is: "So the truth I say, and the truth I say," so both the first and the second "the truth" are in the accusative by "I say," as if you said: "Zaid and 'Amr I struck," so "Zaid and 'Amr" are both accusative by "I struck." So "the truth" and "the truth" are both in the accusative by "I say."

(And it is said: as an absolute object.) He said: "So the truth," that is: "So I establish the truth." On this view it is an absolute object whose governing verb is omitted, its estimate being: "So I establish the truth."

(And it is said: by removing the particle of oath.) That is: "So by the truth I swear," because when the governing particle is removed, the object of the particle becomes accusative. For this reason you often hear them say: "accusative by removal of the governing particle." These are three possibilities. (And its nominative.) Nominative of what? The first "the truth," as a subject whose predicate is omitted, that is: "So the truth is from Me." This is weak.

(And it is said: "So the truth is my oath.") This is less weak than the first. What seems clear to me is that we have no need for this. We say: "the truth" is a subject which contains the meaning of an oath, and it is answered by His words ﴿I will surely fill Hell﴾, and the answer to the oath is sufficient in place of the predicate of the subject. That is, in its i'rab we say: ﴿the truth﴾ is a subject, and it contains the meaning of an oath, and it is answered by His words ﴿I will surely fill﴾, and the answer to the oath suffices in place of the subject's predicate, just as the answer to the oath is dispensed with in place of the answer to the condition when a condition and an oath are combined.

He said: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all of them﴾ [38:85] (that is, mankind). ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾ alone, or is the meaning the genus? The genus. For this reason the author said: (with your offspring). ﴿And with those among them who follow you﴾, that is, mankind, ﴿all of them﴾, whom you swore to mislead. For this reason the Fire is an abode for only two kinds of created beings: the jinn and mankind. The angels are not its people, nor are the beasts, insects and others. Only two kinds of created beings enter the Fire: mankind and the jinn.

He says: ﴿Say: "I do not ask you for any reward for it"﴾ [38:86]. ﴿Say﴾: the address is to the Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿I do not ask you for it﴾, that is, for what I came with and for conveying it. ﴿Any reward﴾: ﴿any﴾ here is extra (za'idah), and ﴿reward﴾ is in the accusative position as a second object, by His words ﴿I ask you﴾. Know that if "sa'ala" (to ask) is followed by "'an" (about), it means enquiry, and if it is followed directly by two objects, it means requesting a gift. So when you say "I asked him about such-and-such," it means enquiry, and when you say "I asked him such-and-such," it is a request for a gift. Here we say: is it a request for a gift or an enquiry? It is a request for a gift, and on this basis ﴿reward﴾ is in the accusative position.

His statement "(a recompense)" is an explanation of ﴿reward﴾, meaning: I do not seek from you that you give me dirhams, or give me sustenance, or marry me to your daughters, or house me in your palaces, in return for conveying the message. Rather, he (ﷺ) seeks his reward from whom? From God.

He said: ﴿And I am not of the pretenders﴾ [38:86] (those who fabricate the Quran from their own selves). That is: and I am not of those who fabricate. But he turned away from "those who fabricate" to ﴿those who pretend (mutakallifin)﴾, because the Quran cannot be produced by a human, even if a person makes an effort and exerts himself; he cannot produce its like. Since this Quran cannot be produced by a human, whoever produces it as a pretender, if he had brought it from himself, is saying: "I do not fabricate the Quran, neither with ease nor with strain."

﴿It is not﴾ [38:87], that is, "the Quran is not." ﴿It is not﴾: he explained it as "is not." We have mentioned a sign of "in" when it means "is not": it is followed by "illa" (except).

﴿It is not, except a reminder﴾ [38:87] (that is, the Quran, a admonition) ﴿to the worlds﴾ (to mankind and the jinn who are rational, not the angels). It is a reminder to the worlds: mankind and the jinn.

As for his statement, "(not the angels)": if he means by excluding the angels that they are not obliged to act upon it, this may be accepted; but if he means that they are not reminded by it and do not draw near to God through it, this is not accepted. For God Most High said: ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder. Whoever wills, let him remember it. In honoured scrolls, exalted, purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾ [80:11–16], and by them are meant the angels.

His words ﴿a reminder to the worlds﴾ [38:87]: the meaning of "reminder" was mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and was mentioned shortly before: ﴿This is a reminder﴾ [38:49]. This is the third occurrence. The meaning is that it is a reminder in itself. What else? Its nobility, and it is a reminder through its admonition.

He says: ﴿It is not, except a reminder to the worlds. And you will surely know its news after a while﴾ [38:87–88] (O disbelievers of Mecca). ﴿Its news﴾: the report of its truthfulness. ﴿After a while﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection.

His words ﴿And you will surely know﴾: he made the pronoun in "you will know" refer to the disbelievers of Mecca, on the basis that the address in this surah is to the people of Mecca, since it is Meccan. But we have mentioned that what matters is the generality of the ruling, not the particularity of place or cause, and the address is to all people: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while﴾ [38:88]. This news which God has announced through this noble Quran, all people will come to know. That is what it reported about what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, for this Quran has reported what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, and all people will come to know this after a while.

In it there are things the Quran reported that have passed and ended; their knowledge comes after a while to those who came after these events and experienced them. In it there are events that will come, which will be known after a while by those who experience them. As for what all people will experience, it is what will happen on the Day of Resurrection.

He said: ﴿After a while﴾ [38:88] (that is, the Day of Resurrection, and "to know" means "to recognise"). Why did he say "'alima" means "'arafa" (to recognise)? Because it has only one object: ﴿And you will surely know its news﴾ [38:88]. When "'alima" takes one object, it means "'arafa," as when you say "I knew the matter," meaning I recognised it. He said: (And the lam before it is the lam of an assumed oath; that is, "By God, you will surely know its news"). And God knows best.

* Shaykh: No, it is one of the creatures of God.

And we gave you an example: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [45:13].
* Student: Shaykh, may God reward you well. A hadith like the hadith: "All flies are in the Fire"[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (13468), and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (9415), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]].

* Shaykh: Let him establish it as coming from the Messenger, and then we will see its status.

* Shaykh: Yes, only the dead person sees it.
* Student: Only?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, those who are with him do not see it, they do not perceive it.

* Shaykh: "Mutakabbir" and "mustakbir"?
* Student: "Mustakbir" and "mutakabbir"?
* Shaykh: "Mustakbir" and "mutakabbir"?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Did it not come in these benefits?
